chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: The block signal payment, Hiram Johnson and Earl Warren as lawyer
summary: Richard received about $400,000 for the block signal with backers from Bisbee, got support from Hiram Johnson, and had Earl Warren as lawyer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

blocks.x: offer...January, '62...don't know what that is. It's too fine for me to read.
It's the automatic safety brake system, filed October 26, 1959.
That's all of this stuff here. And you know, I showed you this, where he had the block signal.
Right. "The semaphore system now used on ..." Part of that's missing. "...cost over $100,000..."

Well, yeah, but he got, I think, $400,000, but he had...he had a coupla fellas that were in on that 'cause they gave him money to build it, you know how that is. It was a couple of saloon men in Bisbee, called the Spires Brothers.
You were telling me--I don't think the tape was on when you told me Hiram Johnson backed him on one of his inventions.

On the...on that...measuring thing for gasoline stations. And you know who his lawyer was in all of that time? Uh... what's the guy went to...got to be head of the Supreme Court...that was from Los Angeles? The Governor of California?

Earl Warren! Earl Warren was his lawyer during all this...inventions, before he got to be governor. Yeah. Yeah, Earl Warren. Ehhh, small world, isn't it? Now, he's got a lot of stuff. This is not...this is just stuff that I happened to know...to find that he...uh, that I didn't give his son, you know, and he had a lot of

inventions that he had patented. Some of 'em he never did do no good with, you know. But he just was full of that stuff, and my brother Johnny was likewise because he never did pay no attention to it. He stuck with music. He had all kinds of ideas--like that Musical Meat Market and things--that was all his ideas, you know, and...
